maui-mahuika-fire.title: A GIFT OF FIRE
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: THE STORY OF FIRE
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: In one telling, Māui wanted to discover the secret of fire. He went to seek out Mahuika, an ancestress who held that powerful gift.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: MEETING MAHUIKA
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: MAHUIKA'S GIFT
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: Mahuika gave Māui a flame from one of her burning fingernails. He carried it away, but his curiosity had not yet been satisfied.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: THE FLAME GOES OUT
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: A VANISHED EMBER
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: Māui deliberately put out the flame and returned to ask for another. Mahuika gave him fire once again, not knowing his purpose.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: BACK FOR MORE
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: THE SAME REQUEST
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: Again and again, Māui extinguished the fire and returned. Each visit brought him another precious flame and tested Mahuika's patience.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: MAHUIKA'S ANGER
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: THE TRICK REVEALED
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: At last Mahuika realized she was being tricked. Her anger grew as Māui's repeated requests threatened the fire she had guarded.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: FIRE IN THE FOREST
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: FLAMES SPREAD
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: Fire swept through the forest, and Māui fled from its danger. In this telling, the gift he had sought had become far too powerful.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: WIND AND RAIN
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: THE STORM ARRIVES
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: Rain and water helped bring the danger to an end in some versions of the story. The flames faded, but the secret of fire was not lost.

maui-mahuika-fire.title: FIRE IN THE TREES
maui-mahuika-fire.caption: FIRE REMAINS
maui-mahuika-fire.narration: In one telling, fire remained within certain trees, ready to be brought forth by friction. Different communities preserve different details of Māui's story.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: SKY AND EARTH
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: RANGINUI AND PAPA
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: One Māori tradition begins with Ranginui, the sky, and Papatūānuku, the earth. Their separation changed the world around their children.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: A GRIEVING MOTHER
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: BENEATH THE LAND
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: After that separation, the children turned their grieving mother Papatūānuku over. In this account, their actions help explain the world beneath us.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: THE CHILD BELOW
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: RŪAUMOKO REMAINS
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: Rūaumoko remained with his mother beneath the earth. His place below the surface became part of the story of the land and its hidden power.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: UNDER OUR FEET
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: A HIDDEN PRESENCE
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: Although he could not be seen above ground, Rūaumoko was still present in the world. The story connects the unseen beneath us with the land.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: THE EARTH STIRS
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: MOVEMENT BELOW
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: In this tradition, Rūaumoko is linked to the movements of the earth. His presence gives the shaking ground a place within a wider story.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: WHEN THE LAND SHAKES
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: EARTHQUAKES
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: Earthquakes are understood in this account through Rūaumoko's movements beneath Papatūānuku. The trembling land becomes part of the pūrākau.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: MOUNTAINS AND FIRE
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: VOLCANIC POWER
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: Rūaumoko is also associated with volcanic activity. The story connects the land's great power with relationships among the atua.

ruaumoko-earthquakes.title: AN ENDURING STORY
ruaumoko-earthquakes.caption: ONE TELLING
ruaumoko-earthquakes.narration: This is one traditional way of understanding earthquakes and volcanoes, not a scientific explanation. Different iwi may tell these stories differently.

rata-and-the-tree.title: THE TREE THAT WOULD NOT STAY DOWN
rata-and-the-tree.caption: BY MORNING, IT STOOD AGAIN
rata-and-the-tree.narration: He cut down the tree. By morning, it was standing again. This is one telling of Rātā and the forest guardians.

rata-and-the-tree.title: A WAKA IN MIND
rata-and-the-tree.caption: THE WORK BEGINS
rata-and-the-tree.narration: Rātā had entered the forest to find timber for a waka. He felled a great tree and began shaping its wood into a canoe.

rata-and-the-tree.title: THE TREE RETURNS
rata-and-the-tree.caption: A STRANGE SIGHT
rata-and-the-tree.narration: When Rātā returned, the tree he had cut was standing tall again. What he had left on the ground seemed to have been restored overnight.

rata-and-the-tree.title: CUT DOWN AGAIN
rata-and-the-tree.caption: THE PUZZLE GROWS
rata-and-the-tree.narration: He cut it down again, but the tree kept returning. Determined to learn why, Rātā hid nearby and watched as darkness settled over the forest.

rata-and-the-tree.title: GUARDIANS AT WORK
rata-and-the-tree.caption: HĀKUTURI
rata-and-the-tree.narration: The hākuturi appeared: forest guardians in the forms of birds, insects, and other living creatures. Together, they restored the tree that Rātā had felled.

rata-and-the-tree.title: A LESSON IN RESPECT
rata-and-the-tree.caption: TIKANGA MATTERS
rata-and-the-tree.narration: Rātā learned that he had not observed the appropriate tikanga when taking a tree. His actions had overlooked the respect owed to the forest.

rata-and-the-tree.title: ANOTHER BEGINNING
rata-and-the-tree.caption: RESPECT FOR THE FOREST
rata-and-the-tree.narration: Rātā then observed the appropriate tikanga and showed respect for the forest. In this telling, the guardians released the tree so he could continue his work.

rata-and-the-tree.title: THE STORY'S MEANING
rata-and-the-tree.caption: CARE FOR NATURE
rata-and-the-tree.narration: The story of Rātā is often remembered as a lesson in caring for the forest. It reminds us that people and the natural world are connected.

tane-three-kete.title: THE SEARCH
tane-three-kete.caption: A QUEST FOR KNOWLEDGE
tane-three-kete.narration: In one tradition, Tāne set out to seek knowledge in the heavens. The journey would link learning, life, and the world of Ranginui above.

tane-three-kete.title: THE JOURNEY BEGINS
tane-three-kete.caption: TOWARD THE HEAVENS
tane-three-kete.narration: Tāne began his ascent toward the heavens, moving beyond the familiar world below. His goal was a source of knowledge of great importance.

tane-three-kete.title: UP THROUGH THE SKY
tane-three-kete.caption: THE HEAVENS ABOVE
tane-three-kete.narration: The story describes a journey through the heavens. In this telling, Tāne climbed toward the highest of twelve heavenly realms.

tane-three-kete.title: THE HIGHEST REALM
tane-three-kete.caption: THE JOURNEY'S END
tane-three-kete.narration: One account names his destination Te Tihi-o-Manono at Te Toi-o-ngā-rangi. These names belong to a tradition of Tāne's search for knowledge.

tane-three-kete.title: THREE BASKETS
tane-three-kete.caption: KETE WĀNANGA
tane-three-kete.narration: Tāne retrieved three baskets of knowledge, called kete wānanga. They became an enduring part of the story of learning and understanding.

tane-three-kete.title: NAMES OF THE KETE
tane-three-kete.caption: THREE KETE
tane-three-kete.narration: The names include te kete-tuatea, te kete-tuauri, and te kete-aronui. Accounts and interpretations of these baskets are not all the same.

tane-three-kete.title: KNOWLEDGE SHARED
tane-three-kete.caption: LEARNING AND LIFE
tane-three-kete.narration: The story links Tāne and Ranginui with knowledge, learning, and the origins of life. It continues to invite reflection on what knowledge means.

tane-three-kete.title: MANY INTERPRETATIONS
tane-three-kete.caption: ONE TRADITION
tane-three-kete.narration: This is one telling of Tāne and the three baskets of knowledge. Different traditions and Māori scholars offer different interpretations.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: THE KNOWLEDGE FROM BELOW
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: A JOURNEY THAT CHANGED TĀ MOKO
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: He entered the world below to find his wife, and returned with the knowledge of tā moko. This is one telling of Mataora and Niwareka.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: NIWAREKA LEAVES
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: A BROKEN RELATIONSHIP
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: Mataora married Niwareka, a woman from Rarohenga. After he struck her in anger, she returned to her people, and he followed in remorse.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: THE JOURNEY BELOW
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: SEEKING NIWAREKA
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: Mataora journeyed into Rarohenga to find Niwareka. There he encountered her father Uetonga, a master of tā moko whose markings would not rub away.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: PAINT AND PERMANENCE
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: UETONGA'S LESSON
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: Uetonga showed how easily Mataora's painted facial designs could be wiped away. Mataora asked to receive lasting moko, and to learn from him.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: RECEIVING MOKO
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: HUMILITY AND REMORSE
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: Receiving moko was painful. In this telling, Niwareka came to see Mataora and recognised the cloak she had woven for him.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: A PROMISE TO CHANGE
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: NIWAREKA'S CHOICE
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: After his face healed, Mataora promised he would never harm Niwareka again. She agreed to return with him to the world above.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: KNOWLEDGE RETURNS
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: TĀ MOKO AND TĀNIKO
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: Mataora carried knowledge of tā moko back to the living world. Niwareka also brought the art of tāniko, a tradition of fine patterned weaving.

mataora-niwareka-moko.title: A LIVING TRADITION
mataora-niwareka-moko.caption: MORE THAN DECORATION
mataora-niwareka-moko.narration: This is one traditional account of tā moko's origins. The art carries identity and meaning, and its stories and practices differ among Māori communities.
